$comment: bops command manifest. Normative; see SPEC.md §4. Changing output shapes, exit semantics, or state conventions bumps `contract`.

json.doc: Emit one JSON document on stdout. Default when stdout is not a TTY.

exit.1: could not run: remote or ledger unreachable, precondition unverifiable, bd error
exit.3: negative verdict on a write: lost or refused, ok:false

commands.name: next

caps.doc: Capabilities this run offers; beads with unmet needs:<cap> are excluded.

include-unworkable.doc: Also return excluded candidates with why_not, and the beads open gates alone keep out of bd ready (W05, blocked_by_gates; not in excluded_count).

avoid-conflicts.doc: Also exclude candidates whose touches:<path> labels overlap a live claim's (advisory; a bead with none never conflicts).

wraps: git fetch refs/bops/claims/* (one round trip, so W14 sees claims the ledger has not caught up with; on failure a warning and the last sync's copy)
with --include-unworkable: bd gate list --limit 0 --json, bd blocked --json, bd show <id> --json (each bead open gates alone hold back)

commands.name: claim
commands.intent: Take this bead for this run

id.doc: The bead to claim. Required unless --next.

force.doc: Take over a claim idle for stale_minutes (default 120), or an orphan. Refused on a landing bead. On success, previous names the last holder, its last note's NEXT/BLOCKER paragraph (note_run), branch and MR, all inferred ledger text.

resume.doc: Take back a landing bead for PR rework, or your own held bead from another machine. Only the ref's actor can.

next.doc: No id: claim the first workable bead in next's order, trying the next on lost, refused, ref_contention or a bead bd cannot show (at most 5 tries, while 30s of budget is left; skipped lists them). Refused, naming them, when the run already holds a bead.

preconditions: an id, or --next and no id (--next takes neither --force nor --resume, and is refused while the run holds any bead)
assignee is empty OR --force
status in (open, ready)
no run: label
no label listed in blocking_labels (config; --force skips it, and a bead this run already holds answers held)
the lock remote (lock.remote, default origin) matches the Dolt remote (lock.mode ref)
no other bops process on this machine is working on the bead (waits up to 10 seconds, then ref_contention)
--resume: the claim ref's actor is this run's, and its state is landing, or held with a machine= that is not this machine (a held ref with no machine= is refused)
wraps: with --next: next's reads, then the steps below per candidate (bead wait 2 seconds)

commands.name: note
commands.intent: Record where I am, keep the claim

op-id.doc: Names this write (op=<id> on its event comment). Running the same op again (same run) writes nothing and answers with replayed:true, so a write that hit a busy bead, a rejected push, a timeout or a lost answer is simply re-run. Default: derived from command, bead, run and content.

preconditions: this run holds the bead and its ref still matches
no other bops process on this machine is working on the bead (waits up to 10 seconds, then ref_contention)
lint: last paragraph starts with NEXT:|BLOCKER:|KEY DECISION:|REF: (warn)
wraps: git push refs/bops/claims/<id> (lease; a network failure is a warning)

commands.name: renew

id.doc: The bead to renew; the command line takes several, space-separated, each with its own outcome. Run as the run that claimed (the same checkout and BOPS_RUN). On any non-zero exit, read beads[].outcome: a run with a bead not refreshed exits 1 even when another is lost.

preconditions: the claim lock is on (lock.mode is not none)
this run holds the bead and its ref still matches (an invalid id is refused, code bad_id)
the hold has a claim ref: one taken before the claim lock is refused, code legacy_hold
no other bops process on this machine is working on the bead (waits up to 10 seconds, then ref_contention)
never: write the ledger (no comment, no bd heartbeat)
wraps: git push refs/bops/claims/<id> (lease), per bead; after an unreachable or git_auth failure the rest are not tried
git push (lease): delete the ref of a release whose delete never finished, as note does

commands.name: release

text.doc: Optional. Read only when asked: --file <path>, or --file - for stdin. Never on the command line. Recorded below the event line of the release's bops:released comment; a lost or refused release writes none of it.

op-id.doc: As for note. Replays only once this run no longer holds the bead, with the same reason, and pushes the ledger again; a release still held runs in full.

preconditions: this run holds the bead and its ref still matches
done: the bead has a landed record (bops land first); else refused, before the ref or the ledger changes
no other bops process on this machine is working on the bead (waits up to 10 seconds, then ref_contention)
wraps: bd comments <id> --json (op id check, when not held)
git push (lease): state=landing on done, delete otherwise
bd comments add <id> <event> (no text), or bd comments add <id> -f <file> (event line, then the --file text)

commands.name: land
commands.intent: Record that work reached its destination

op-id.doc: As for note. A repeat of the same ref and sha adds no record; the op id also answers one retried after the release. A replay pushes the ledger again.

preconditions: this run holds the bead and its ref still matches
no other bops process on this machine is working on the bead (waits up to 10 seconds, then ref_contention)
never: merge
push a branch
close
wraps: bd comments <id> --json (op id check, when not held or a repeat)

commands.name: sweep
commands.intent: Close landed beads whose refs are merged
never: skip a bops:landing bead with no landed record (it is listed under unknown)
wait for a bead another bops process on this machine is working on (it is listed under unknown)
close a bead that changed since sweep read it: re-held, resumed or given back (it is listed under pending)
wraps: bd label remove <id> bops:landing (after the close; a failure is a warning)

commands.name: stale

older-than.doc: Idle longer than this is stale; defaults to the stale_minutes config (120). Age is from the claim ref's at, which note refreshes; a claim with no ref uses updated_at, heartbeat_at and its newest bops: comment.

all-machines.doc: false hides claims and orphans from other machines.

wraps: git fetch --prune refs/bops/claims/* (the last sync's copy if offline, with a warning)

commands.name: status

mine.doc: Only claims made on this machine (same_machine: a run of this clone, or a ref or bops:claimed comment naming this machine).

stale.doc: Only stale, orphan and unknown claims (unknown: staleness could not be judged, so it may be stale). A held ref that is stale and does not match its ledger claim is one orphan row, where stale lists it under both.

older-than.doc: Idle longer than this is stale, as for stale.

never: write the ledger or a ref
call a claim stale when stale would not: a ref whose state or at is unreadable or whose at is in the future, or a no-ref claim whose comments could not be read, is unknown
ask the forge: branch and mr are inferred from branch names and the ledger, as claim --force's previous infers them
wraps: git fetch --prune refs/bops/claims/* (the last sync's copy if offline, with a warning)

commands.name: reap
commands.intent: Release stale claims that hold no work
preconditions: the claim lock is on (lock.mode is not none)
a Dolt remote on the lock remote's repository (not with --dry-run)
--older-than, when given, is at least stale_minutes

older-than.doc: Idle longer than this is stale, as for stale; shorter than stale_minutes is refused.

only.doc: Comma-separated bead ids, normally the ones a preview listed under would_release: act on these only. <id>@<run> also pins the holder the preview showed: a claim held now by another run is listed under skipped, not released. One that is no longer a stale claim is listed under skipped; an empty list is a usage error. A claim made outside bops (no run label, no ref) is released only when named here.

forge.doc: Forge searched for open or merged merge requests naming each claim with no other evidence; none searches nothing, with a warning.

never: release a claim labelled needs-land, with a merge request on the bead (a URL, with or without its scheme, or PR #N, MR !N or !N), held by a live worktree of this clone, or whose bead id is carried by a branch name (lock remote, origin, local, or a worktree's branch or directory; a short number after the id's prefix with a dot on both sides is taken for a version, not the id) or by the title or branch of a merge request, not closed unmerged, that the forge's search of titles and descriptions finds; it is listed under kept with what was found
release a claim when the forge search fails, takes longer than 20 s, or returns a full page (100) without a match; it is kept as forge unanswered, with a warning naming --forge none
release a claim whose merge request the forge finds after its takeover (the search runs again under the bead lock; this run keeps it, listed under failed with outcome held)
release anything when the ledger pull or the first branch listing fails; a later listing failure stops the run, listing the rest under skipped
release a claim made outside bops (no run label, no ref) unless --only names it
release a claim whose evidence appears after its takeover (this run keeps it, listed under failed with outcome held)

start a takeover with less than 200 s of the command's time left (90 s for it, 30 s for the evidence re-read, 20 s for the forge search after it, 60 s for its release, each on its own clock; the rest are listed under skipped)
release a claim refreshed since stale read it (claim --force re-checks under a lease)
report as failed a claim released, taken over or refreshed by someone else since it was judged (listed under skipped; the run is negative only when --only named it)
keep a claim because the command's deadline cut its evidence read or forge search short (it and the rest are listed under skipped, to run again)
release a claim another run holds than the one stale read, or than --only <id>@<run> named (claim --force re-checks the run on the read its lease is taken on)
touch an orphan ref (a ref with no claim on the ledger)
let another bops process in this clone, sync included, act on a claim between its takeover and its release (one bead lock covers both)
delete a released claim's ref before its ledger push lands (until then the ref stays, release pending, and the next sync or command on the bead pushes, then deletes it)
wraps: git remote (when the lock remote is not origin)
git ls-remote --heads <lock remote> (and origin, when it exists)
git for-each-ref refs/heads refs/remotes (local branches, and other remotes as of their last fetch)
forge search for <id> in titles and descriptions (gh pr list --search, or the GitLab merge requests API), for a claim with no other evidence, before and after its takeover

commands.name: gc
commands.intent: Delete refs of closed beads and orphans
preconditions: the claim lock is on (lock.mode is not none)
a Dolt remote on the lock remote's repository (not with --dry-run)

only.doc: Comma-separated bead ids, normally the ones a preview listed under would_delete: act on these only. One whose ref is no longer one gc deletes is listed under skipped; one with no ref at all is a warning; an empty list is a usage error.

never: delete a ref whose bead is not closed and carries a claim by the ref's run or actor (in progress, or parked blocked or deferred; a parked one is listed under kept), or a landing ref of a bead in progress (sweep's)

delete an orphan younger than stale_minutes, or a closed bead's ref younger than stale_minutes written later than 15 minutes before the bead's last ledger change (a claim whose ledger write may be pending, allowing for clock skew); the latter is listed under kept
delete anything when the ledger pull or the ref fetch fails
delete a ref a hold of this clone names, or whose bead changed since gc read it (re-read from the ledger as pulled, under the bead lock; listed under kept)
delete a ref re-taken since gc read it (the delete leases the sha it read; listed under failed)
wait for a bead another bops process on this machine is working on (listed under failed)
delete or keep a ref whose bead could not be read, or that the command's time ran out before judging (listed under failed)
write the ledger
wraps: git fetch --prune refs/bops/claims/* (not with --dry-run; stale's copy otherwise)
bd show <id> --json (each ref's bead; again under the bead lock)

commands.name: sync
commands.intent: Pull, heartbeat, push — with the one retry
wraps: bd update <id> --assignee <actor> --status in_progress --force, or --assignee alone on a blocked or deferred bead (this run's live claims whose display differs)
bd heartbeat <id> (this run's live claims only; another run's are settled against their refs but not re-displayed or heartbeat)
bd update <id> --assignee '' --status open; bd label remove <id> run:<ulid> (this run's claim whose ref is gone and that nobody took)

commands.name: session-start

hook-json.doc: Print the document as Claude Code SessionStart hook output ({hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName,additionalContext}}) and always exit 0, so the harness injects it.

wraps: sync --no-push, for this run's holds only (another run's stranded hold is listed, nothing else of another run's is touched); its bd dolt pull ends 25 s before the 60 s budget, so the rest still reports

commands.name: guard
commands.intent: Refuse a raw bd claim before it runs

command.doc: The shell command to check. Without --hook-json only.

hook-json.doc: Read Claude Code's PreToolUse payload ({tool_name, tool_input:{command}, cwd}) on stdin instead, and always exit 0: a refusal prints {hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:PreToolUse, permissionDecision:deny, permissionDecisionReason}}, anything else prints nothing, so the harness's own permission rules still apply.

preconditions: refuses only in a worktree with a .beads directory, or whose main checkout has one (the worktree holding the payload cwd, else the current directory), and whose claim lock is on (lock.mode is not none); every other case allows
never: run bd or touch the network: its one subprocess is git rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-common-dir, to find the worktree and its main checkout, cut off after 2 s (then the directory itself is used)
refuse when it cannot decide (unreadable input or config allows the command, with a warning: it fails open)
print an allow decision, which would skip the harness's permission prompt
wraps: finds bd update ... --claim, bd ready ... --claim and bd reclaim in each simple command (after ;, &&, ||, |, subshells, command substitution, also inside double quotes, leading assignments and wrappers such as env and timeout, sh -c and eval), skipping quoted text, comments, heredoc bodies, shifts inside (( )) and --help calls; variables, aliases, sourced scripts and a script on a shell's stdin are not read

output.matched: string (the raw claim found: bd update --claim, bd ready --claim or bd reclaim; empty when none)
output.use: string (the bops command to run instead; empty unless refused)
output.reason: string (the refusal the agent sees; empty unless refused)

commands.name: doctor
commands.intent: Can the claim lock work against its remote (lock.remote, default origin)?
never: write a claim ref or the ledger
leave its probe ref behind silently (a failed delete is a warning naming the command)
wraps: lock: git push (create-only) refs/bops/doctor/<nonce>, then a second create-only push that must be refused
git push (lease): delete the probe ref
dolt_remote: bd dolt remote list --json (a Dolt remote on the lock remote's repository, else remote_mismatch)

blocking_labels: bd list --all --include-gates --limit 0 --json, once, when blocking_labels are set: a label no bead carries, matched exactly, is a warning, and a list bd cannot give is a not-checked warning, neither a failed check
git log -1 -- bops/ and git merge-base --is-ancestor, only in bops's own source checkout: a binary built before the last bops/ commit is a warning, not a failed check
bops_version: only when .bops.json sets min_bops: this bops older than it fails (bops_too_old), and a build with no version is a warning

output.failed: string[] (any entry: exit 1, code from the first failure)

commands.name: gates
commands.intent: What is blocking this bead's path?
wraps: bd gate list <id> --all --json (satisfied: the gate is closed)
bd dep list <id> --json (blocking_deps: open blocks-type deps that are not gates; parent-child is not one)

commands.name: deps
wraps: bd list --all --include-gates --limit 0 --json (engine=bd: one call; the graph is the beads not closed, joined by blocks, conditional-blocks and waits-for edges; parent-child is not one; a blocker the list hides counts as open)
depth and critical_path: the longest chain of open beads ending at <id>, by Kahn's algorithm in Go; a cycle among the beads <id> waits on exits 1 naming it

bd sql --json <recursive CTE> (engine=cte: needs bd in server mode and exits 1 on an embedded ledger; one query for the closure and the longest chain to each bead, and a second only to name a cycle; Go walks the chain with engine=bd's tie-break, so the answer is engine=bd's)
engine=graph: reserved, exits 1 as not implemented

commands.name: version
commands.intent: Report bops, contract, and detected bd

output.revision: string (the commit this binary was built from; empty when the go command recorded none)
output.modified: bool (built from a tree with uncommitted changes)
output.revision_time: string (that commit's time, RFC 3339; empty with no revision)
